blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Altamont condos

items.t: Where condo stock would concentrate in West Vancouver — the Ambleside waterfront and town centre and the Dundarave village edge — is outside Altamont.

Main streets: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route below the area, Queens Avenue climbs the hillside, and Taylor Way connects Marine Drive to Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway); the Lions Gate Bridge is the fixed crossing to Vancouver.

Transit anchors: TransLink route 251 (Queens / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside, and route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge. There is no rapid transit and no condo node inside Altamont.

blocks.text: Good to know about Altamont condos

items.t: The density rules changed under the area on July 21, 2025. The Province directed West Vancouver to increase density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Dundarave by December 31, 2025 — Altamont's lower streets are exactly that adjacency, so infill potential quoted from older material may already be stale.

Two hazard permits ride on hillside lots. Work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface needs a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit, and work within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank needs an Environmental Development Permit; a Foreshore Development Permit applies to waterfront or coastal-flood-risk property on the lowest streets.

The seawalk below the hill dates to Canada's centennial. The Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 and runs roughly 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park (150 25th Street, with more than 50 metres of sandy beach) to Ambleside — the waterfront amenity for an area that has no park confirmed inside its own lines.

The RS zone range is extreme. Minimum site areas in the zones that can apply run from 488 m² (RS5) to 8,094 m² (RS1) — two Altamont lots on adjoining streets can carry completely different subdivision and suite potential, confirmed only on the District's Zoning Map.
Westerleigh PARC is a rental residence. It shows up in West Vancouver attached-housing searches, but there is nothing to buy.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Altamont townhomes

items.t: Main roads: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route below the area; Queens Avenue climbs the hillside; Taylor Way connects Marine Drive to Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway), and the Lions Gate Bridge is the fixed crossing to Vancouver.

Transit: route 251 (Queens / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside, running from Marine Drive at 25th Street to Park Royal via 27th Street, Queens Avenue, 15th Street, Mathers Avenue, Burley Drive, Kings Avenue, 11th Street, Fulton Avenue and 17th Street; route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via Georgia Street, the Stanley Park Causeway and the Lions Gate Bridge.

Schools: School District 45 catchments are address-based and SD45 directs families to the school locator. SD45 has no middle tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grade 8 to Grade 12. Nearby: Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue, in Dundarave; Westcot Elementary (K–7) at the foot of the British Properties; West Vancouver Secondary, 1750 Mathers Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Altamont

items.t: The governing pair is West Vancouver's own: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, District of West Vancouver. White Rock's 2506/2220 pair is never attributed to West Vancouver.

If a strata townhouse is ever found on this hillside, the BC standard block applies in full: Form B diligence (Strata Property Act s. 59 — fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page).

Rental and age bylaws: rental-restriction bylaws are void since Nov 24, 2022 — any directory "rentals not allowed" line for a West Vancouver strata is void for long-term rentals (short-term rentals can still be restricted); only 55+ age bylaws are valid since Nov 24, 2022 (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023). No Altamont complex exists to apply either rule to today.

Fee-simple reality in Altamont: the stock is fee-simple detached — no strata, no Form B, no strata fees — governed by municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 4662) and any registered covenants on title only. Secondary suites and a detached secondary suite are permitted uses in the single-family zones, subject to the bylaw's conditions.

Provincial density directive: on July 21, 2025, the Province directed West Vancouver to amend its OCP to provide increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave (and at Park Royal–Taylor Way) by December 31, 2025 — Altamont sits directly above Dundarave, so infill rules on its lower streets are in transition and must be verified per property.

Hazards: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface — both can apply on Altamont's hillside and creek lots; a Foreshore Development Permit can apply to the lowest streets below the hillside.

blocks.text: Good to know about Altamont townhomes

items.t: Altamont is not an official District name. The OCP's structure is Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay — "Altamont" is a site/listing name for the hillside between Dundarave and Caulfeild, with no published street boundaries. Two agents can draw its lines differently and both be working from the same absence.

The seawalk below the hillside dates to Canada's centennial. The Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 and runs roughly 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park to Ambleside, below the Altamont hillside; Dundarave Park, 150 25th Street, has more than 50 metres of sandy beach, a playground, washrooms and a seasonal concession.

The District's main indoor facilities are in Ambleside, not on the hill: the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive, and the West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive — the library opened as a War Memorial, dedicated to those who served in the Second World War.
West Vancouver's 2021 Census population was 44,122 (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile) — District context for a hillside pocket with no centre of its own.
Utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — a carrying-cost difference from flat-fee municipalities that hillside buyers rarely budget for.

RS hillside lot fabric: detached houses on hillside lots in the RS single-family dwelling zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010. Section 200 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS6 using the area of the site of record. The RS range that can apply here runs the full 488–8,094 m² ladder, so subdivision and suite potential differ lot by lot — the zone and minimum for a specific lot are confirmed on the District's Zoning Map. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Suites as lot value: Section 200 lists secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among permitted uses in the single-family zones; District building-permit guidance addresses detached secondary suites (coach houses) as a permitted form on these lots.

Hazard-shaped land: this hillside's buildable value is permit-shaped — Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area ground (within 100 m of an undisturbed forest interface), watercourse setbacks (15 m from the top of a bank), and, on the lowest streets below the hillside, the Foreshore Development Permit Area. Gross lot area is not buildable area here.

Provincial density directive (July 21, 2025) — direction, not a rezoning: the Province directed West Vancouver to amend its OCP to provide increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave (and at Park Royal–Taylor Way) by December 31, 2025. Altamont sits directly above Dundarave, so infill rules on its lower streets are in transition. No lot is presented as rezoned on this basis.
Separately from the zero known presale projects of any kind inside Altamont.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Altamont lots

items.t: Municipality: District of West Vancouver, BC — Altamont is a residential hillside area of the District, above Marine Drive between Dundarave to the east and Caulfeild to the west; District-wide land use is guided by the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018.

Roads and transit: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route below the area; Queens Avenue climbs the hillside; Taylor Way connects Marine Drive to Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway), and the Lions Gate Bridge is the fixed crossing to Vancouver. Route 251 (Queens / Park Royal, West Vancouver Blue Bus) serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside; route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver. Most Altamont streets are a hill walk or a drive from transit, the seawalk and Dundarave village.

Schools: SD45 (West Vancouver Schools) catchments are address-based and SD45 directs families to its locator. SD45 has no middle tier (K–7 elementary, 8–12 secondary). Nearby schools: Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue, in Dundarave; Westcot Elementary (K–7), described by SD45 as at the foot of the British Properties; West Vancouver Secondary, 1750 Mathers Avenue.

Services are below the hill: Dundarave Park, 150 25th Street (50+ metres of sandy beach, at the east end of the Centennial Seawalk, built 1967, running ~1.7 km east to Ambleside); West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive; West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive; Park Royal, at Marine Drive and Taylor Way, is the OCP's regional shopping centre. Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Altamont

items.t: Zoning + OCP (District): Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 (s.200 RS minimums in Sections 1–2; lot zone on the District Zoning Map) and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018. White Rock's bylaws (Zoning 2024 No. 2506 / OCP 2017 No. 2220) belong to white rock only and are never imported here.

SSMUH / ground-oriented density, as the bylaw states it: 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop (Bylaw 4662, ss.620–630). Verify current infill zoning per property before marketing multiplex potential on the lower streets.

Hazard development permits — the hillside rules: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank; a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface — both can apply on Altamont's hillside and creek lots and can add geotechnical and permit cost to a rebuild. A Foreshore Development Permit is required for work within the Foreshore Development Permit Area (waterfront property or property at risk of coastal flooding), which can apply to the lowest streets below the hillside.

Strata block: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions. A listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

PTT on land + the additional school tax that actually bites here: PTT general tiers 1% / 2% / 3% + further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000; first-time buyer and newly built home exemptions are home-purchase exemptions as BC states them. Budget for it in closing math where the residential assessment exceeds $3 million.

blocks.text: Good to know about Altamont lots

items.t: "Altamont" is a page name, not a District name. The District's OCP never names it — its structure is Ambleside Town Centre, Park Royal, and the Dundarave / Caulfeild Village / Horseshoe Bay village centres. A buyer searching District documents for "Altamont" zoning or boundaries will find nothing; the operative documents are the District-wide OCP 4985 and Zoning Bylaw 4662, read lot by lot.

The hillside's permit map matters more than its street map: the wildfire-interface line (100 m), the watercourse line (15 m from a bank top) and the foreshore area on the lowest streets each re-price what a lot can actually be built into — two lots on the same street can sit in different permit regimes.

Altamont's lower streets are the ones the Province named: the July 21, 2025 directive singled out the single-family/duplex areas adjacent to Dundarave — the ground directly below this hillside — for increased density by December 31, 2025.

The seawalk below the hill is a centennial artifact: the Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 for Canada's centennial and runs ~1.7 km from Dundarave Park to Ambleside — the waterfront amenity that anchors the hillside's value is public parkland, not lot frontage.

No market figure exists to quote for this hillside: West Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage entirely, so any Altamont median, ratio or trend figure attributed to SnapStats anywhere should be treated as an error.

Altamont is a residential hillside in the District of West Vancouver, above Marine Drive between Dundarave to the east and Caulfeild to the west, below the British Properties.

The District publishes no street-by-street boundary and no Official Community Plan (OCP) neighbourhood name for Altamont; the District's named centres are Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay.
The streets buyers use to place it are the avenues climbing from Marine Drive toward Queens Avenue, with Gisby Street holding the neighbourhood park named in.
Altamont's homes are detached houses on hillside lots in the RS single-family dwelling zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010.
No condominium building or townhome complex inside Altamont was confirmed on a District, developer or strata source; the confirmed stock is freehold detached houses.
Secondary suites and a detached secondary suite (coach house) are among the permitted uses the bylaw lists for the single-family zones.

Altamont's lot-by-lot question is which RS zone applies: minimum site areas run from 488 square metres (m²) in RS5 to 8,094 m² in RS1, with RS2 at 1,625 m², RS3 at 975 m² and RS4 at 731 m²; the District's Zoning Map confirms the zone for a specific lot.

The bylaw's ground-oriented dwelling rules allow 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop: the Province directed the District on July 21, 2025 to increase density in areas adjacent to Dundarave by December 31, 2025, and Altamont sits directly above Dundarave.

blocks.text: Altamont: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Altamont Park is a District neighbourhood park: the District's Parks Master Plan lists Altamont Park among its neighbourhood parks and in its park-protection schedule.

The closest District waterfront park is Dundarave Park, 150 25th Street, with more than 50 metres of sandy beach at the east end of the Centennial Seawalk, which runs about 1.7 kilometres east to Ambleside.

The District's main indoor recreation facility serving Altamont is the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive, and its library is West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive, both in Ambleside.

Provincial density directive for the Dundarave-adjacent single-family and duplex areas, including Altamont's lower streets: the Province directed OCP amendments for increased density by December 31, 2025.

The Altamont-relevant extra is the Province's additional school tax, which can apply at this hillside's assessment levels: 0.2 percent on the residential portion between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4 percent above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3 and 0.6 percent on January 1, 2027.

Route 251 Queens / Park Royal, operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside, running from Marine Drive at 25th Street to Park Royal via 27th Street, Queens Avenue, 15th Street, Mathers Avenue, Burley Drive, Kings Avenue, 11th Street, Fulton Avenue and 17th Street.

Wildfire interface: the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, approved December 14, 2020, covers properties within 100 metres of a forested area — about 50 percent of District land — and a permit is needed before constructing most new homes and coach houses in it.

Creeks: in Existing Neighbourhoods, development within 15 metres of the top of bank of a watercourse requires an Environmental Development Permit, and development is defined to include vegetation removal, soil disturbance and hazard-tree work.
Foreshore: tree work within 15 metres of the natural boundary (high tide mark) of the ocean needs a foreshore tree permit, relevant to Altamont's lowest Marine Drive lots.

Confirm the lot's RS zone and permit areas on the District's Zoning Map and WESTMap before relying on suite, coach-house or subdivision potential; the map, not the street's largest homes, states the entitlement.

blocks.text: Between Dundarave village and the British Properties, with the seawalk and Marine Drive just below, Altamont is a hillside address.

faq.a: A "condo" search result carrying an Altamont label should be checked for whether the property is actually in Ambleside or Dundarave.
faq.q: Are there any condos for sale in Altamont itself?

faq.a: In the District's centres named in the OCP — the Ambleside Municipal Town Centre and the Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay village centres — not on the Altamont hillside. The best-known waterfront building below the area, Villa Maris, is in Dundarave.
faq.q: Where is the nearest real condo stock?

faq.a: No. Secondary suites and detached secondary suites are permitted uses in the RS zones, but they are accessory to the detached lot — they are not separate strata lots and cannot be bought on their own title. The ground-oriented rules allow 4 dwellings per lot, or 6 within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop, still as one lot's ownership unless a future rezoning and stratification occur.
faq.q: Can I buy a suite or coach house separately in Altamont?

faq.a: Not for a long-term tenancy — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, whatever a building directory still shows. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind, and a 55+ age bylaw can still limit who may live in the unit.
faq.q: If I buy a condo in Ambleside or Dundarave instead, can the strata ban rentals?

faq.a: There is no strata, so there is no Form B, depreciation report or CRF to review. The equivalent checks are the lot's RS zone and minimum site area on the District's Zoning Map, and the hazard permit areas (wildfire interface, watercourse setback, foreshore) that can apply to hillside and creek lots.
faq.q: What replaces the Form B diligence for an Altamont house purchase?

faq.a: The area is detached houses in the RS single-family zones. A "townhouse" search result carrying an Altamont label should be checked for whether the property is actually in Ambleside, Dundarave or Caulfeild.
faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Altamont?

faq.a: The Altamont hillside itself contributes none.
faq.q: Where is the nearest real townhouse stock?

faq.a: No. A detached secondary suite (coach house) is a permitted second unit on a fee-simple detached lot under Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 — no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.
faq.q: Is a coach house the same as a townhouse here?

faq.a: Not in the District's plan. The name is used for this hillside in property searches, but it does not appear as a named neighbourhood in the District's Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, whose centres are Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay. Plan and permit questions for an Altamont lot are answered at District level, not by a local area plan.
faq.q: Is Altamont an official West Vancouver neighbourhood?

faq.a: Only the locator can say. School District No. 45 (SD45), West Vancouver Schools, sets catchments by address and directs families to the school locator on its admissions page. The nearest elementary schools by address are West Bay Elementary, Kindergarten to Grade 7, at 3175 Thompson Place to the west, and Irwin Park Elementary in Dundarave to the east; neither is confirmed as the catchment for a specific Altamont address.
faq.q: Which school will an Altamont address feed into?

faq.a: Possibly, within two layers of rules. The lot's RS zone and the post-directive amendments decide the real number.
faq.q: Can I add a coach house or extra dwellings on an Altamont lot?

faq.a: They can, and both triggers are measured in metres. An Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface. On a sloped, treed Altamont lot, either trigger can add a qualified professional and permit time to a rebuild.
faq.q: Do creek or wildfire permits affect a rebuild here?

faq.a: West Vancouver Schools (SD45) directs families to the school locator tool on its admissions page; catchments are address-based, and no Altamont catchment is confirmed here — check the exact address in the locator. SD45 has no middle schools: elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12.
faq.q: How do I find the catchment school for an Altamont address?

faq.a: Route 251 (Queens / Park Royal) on Queens Avenue below the hillside, and route 250 on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge.
faq.q: Which buses serve the Altamont area?

faq.a: The RS single-family dwelling zones in Section 200 of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010, with minimum site areas from 488 m² (RS5) to 8,094 m² (RS1), and secondary suites and detached secondary suites among the permitted uses.
faq.q: What zoning covers houses in Altamont?
